intent: The last row still wearing the old shape gets the new one, so the two rows a user meets on this single route stop disagreeing about what a confirmation looks like.
rationale:
This is the row DT-0016 could not reach, and the reason is worth keeping: it was not modelled. `perform-deploy` was a component in the surface manifest and got the treatment; this row existed only as a sentence inside `button-secondary`'s description, so no ticket could name it and no design round could see it. It was surveyed as `deploy-chooser-row` on 2026-08-13, and the page now carries that id in a comment — `validate` refuses a component whose id appears in no source file, which is the check that would have caught the omission a month earlier.

The two rows sit on **one route**. A user names a market in this row, and meets `perform-deploy` on the next request. Today the first wraps and the second stacks full-width under `tablet`, so the same page changes its mind about confirmation layout between two steps of one task. That is worse than the uniform wrongness that preceded DT-0016, because a reader has to work out whether the difference is deliberate.

No new treatment. DT-0016 settled it; this is the last surface spending it, which is why it is p3 and why the acceptance is a comparison rather than a measurement.

One thing deliberately left alone: both controls stay `BUTTON_SECONDARY`. This form asks — it composes a description and reaches no operation — and `control.ts` keeps the primary weight for the page that follows. Restacking a row is layout; changing which weight it wears would be saying the page commits something, and it does not.

design.layout: The row becomes `flex flex-col gap-3` below the tablet breakpoint and `tablet:flex-row tablet:flex-wrap` at and above it, matching DT-0016 exactly. Both controls take `w-full tablet:w-auto`. The two labelled fields above the row keep their own `space-y-3` stacking and are not touched — they are part of the form, not part of this row.

default.content: The GET submit ('See what deploying would do') first, then the anchor back to the agent, stacked full-width under tablet and inline above it. Submit first in both, matching every other confirmation row on the product: the reading order does not change with the viewport.

not-rendered-without-timeframes.content: Nothing to restyle. When BattleGrid declares no permitted timeframes the whole form is replaced by a role=alert sentence saying a deployment cannot be composed, so this row does not render at all. Recorded rather than skipped so a reader checking this ticket against the manifest finds the state accounted for instead of wondering whether it was missed — and so nobody adds a dimmed row here, which the system's own principle forbids where retrying cannot help.

responsive.mobile: Stacked, each control full width, in reading order.
responsive.desktop: A wrapping row at natural widths.

acceptance: Below breakpoint.tablet the submit and the anchor are each full width and stacked vertically, with space.3 between them.
At and above breakpoint.tablet they sit on one wrapping row at natural widths.
Rendered at both viewports beside this same route's proposal branch, the chooser row and perform-deploy are indistinguishable in layout.
Both controls still wear BUTTON_SECONDARY — neither is promoted to primary.
The submit remains inside the method="get" form and is not converted to a server action.
The two labelled fields above the row keep their existing stacking, unchanged at both viewports.
Both controls meet size.control.min in both layouts.
No raw pixel value for the breakpoint or the gap appears in the component.
references: src/presentation/components/control.ts — primary is the action the page exists to offer; secondary is every submit that only asks
